slides.say: You write onClick on a button. But React does not attach a listener to that button.

slides.text: React attaches one handler per event type at the top, then "bubbles" the event through your components.
slides.say: For most events, React attaches one handler per event type at the top, then figures out which components to call. That is event delegation.
Up to React sixteen, that top was the document. Since React seventeen, it is the root DOM container your app renders into.

slides.text: So stopPropagation works with other code on the page, and React versions can nest.
slides.say: This makes stop propagation behave as expected with non React code on the page, and lets apps on different React versions nest safely.
